Section A — STEELMAN.text: This is the right opener because it is the actual Savvas Model & Discuss launch for 4-3 (`a2_4-3_SE.tex:36-50`; `questionbank/registry.jsonl:43`), so it satisfies `CLAUDE.md:8` while matching the observation-template need for a visual first task. For an ELL-heavy small class (`CLAUDE.md:97`), starting with a familiar line and then excluding one x-value isolates the new idea: domain restriction. It also cleanly establishes the day’s throughline. Parts A/B/C move from domain to excluded value to function type, which is exactly the bridge into rational expressions and fits the Do Now phase in `CLAUDE.md:14`.

#35 is a defensible Apply choice because the source is exact Savvas (`a2_4-3_SE.tex:478-487`; `a2_4-3_TE.tex:1000-1033`; `questionbank/registry.jsonl:80`) and the formulas are printed, so students spend time substituting, simplifying, and comparing rather than waiting on teacher exposition. That is good observation-day design for a solo teacher. Even though Savvas tags it DOK 1, using it as the Apply slot is still reasonable: it is not the spine, it is the bridge from symbolic simplification to contextual ratios, which sets up #36 well.

#36 is the strongest place to house the one spine. The Savvas core is exact (`a2_4-3_SE.tex:492-495`; `a2_4-3_TE.tex:1036-1050`; `questionbank/registry.jsonl:81`), and the context forces students to build a rational expression from geometry rather than just simplify a given one. That makes the hidden domain idea visible. For an observation, this is also the best evidence of student thinking: build, simplify, and interpret is the cleanest place to show strategic reasoning under `CLAUDE.md:9`, even if Savvas itself labels the base item DOK 2.

Ending with #13 is intellectually coherent because it pulls the class from procedure back to structure. It is the actual Savvas closure question (`a2_4-3_SE.tex:352-355`; `a2_4-3_TE.tex:800-803`; `questionbank/registry.jsonl:58`), and the sentence frames at `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:258-263` honor the ELL requirement in `CLAUDE.md:97`. The reflection prompts also match the DOCX closeout, so the design logic is strong even though the compliance risk is real.

Section B — RISKS.risk: `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:251-263` creates a second DOK-3 center. Savvas marks #13 as DOK 3 at `a2_4-3_TE.tex:800-803`, the registry marks it `role: dok3-driver` at `questionbank/registry.jsonl:58`, and the pilot tags do the same at `tagging/4-3_pilot.jsonl:15`. If `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:190-230` is already the period spine, the exit now violates both the single-spine rule (`CLAUDE.md:9`) and the summary-exit rule (`CLAUDE.md:10`).

`tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:177` and `:215-230` add student-facing prompts that are not in the Savvas wording for #35/#36. Compare with `a2_4-3_SE.tex:485-487,492-495` and `a2_4-3_TE.tex:1027-1033,1036-1050`. Under `CLAUDE.md:8`, “What does that mean about the design?”, “state the domain restrictions in this physical situation”, and the `x = 4` fairness prompt do not trace cleanly.

ELL support is back-loaded. The only printed frames are at `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:258-263`, but the longest explanation demands happen earlier at `:114-117`, `:177-180`, and `:222-234`. That is thin for an ELL-heavy class under `CLAUDE.md:97`.

The pacing is defensible but too implicit. The file comments allocate 10 + 15 + 20 + 5 minutes at `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:75`, `:122`, `:185`, and `:239`, which leaves 15 minutes unaccounted for and no visible share/summary cue, even though `CLAUDE.md:14` requires one.

There is minor DOCX drift at `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:126`: the heading uses a bullet, while the template text reads “Apply – Make Sense and Persevere.” Small, but easy for an observer to notice because the rest of the packet is clearly mirroring that format.
`tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:114-117` is slightly too open. “What kind of function” may elicit “a line with a hole” instead of the denominator-restriction insight the packet wants.

Section C — FIXES.fix: Make `#36` the only spine. Replace the exit prompt at `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:251-263` with Savvas #14 from `a2_4-3_TE.tex:806-807`: “Explain why domain restrictions are necessary to show that the rational expressions (-6x^2+21x)/(3x) and -2x+7 are equivalent. What is true about the graphs at x=0 and why?” That keeps the exit on the day’s throughline but removes the second official DOK-3 driver.

Restore strict Savvas traceability on the student page. At `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:177`, delete “What does that mean about the design?” At `:215-230`, revert to the exact #36 ask: “Find the ratio that represents this probability in simplified form.” Move the domain/fairness probes to teacher notes or slides. If you want the A/B/C scaffold to remain student-facing, bank those derived prompts first; otherwise they are fabricated items under `CLAUDE.md:8`.

Add earlier frames, not just exit frames. After `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:114`, insert a starter like: “I think the graph could come from ____ because x = ____ is excluded.” After `:222`, insert: “The value x = ____ is excluded because the original denominator would be zero.” After `:230`, insert: “When x = 4, the probability is ____, so the game is fair / unfair because ____.”

Make the phase plan explicit outside the student sheet. In the teacher pacing note, lock this to 10 Do Now, 10-12 Apply-as-launch, 23-25 Performance explore, 10 share/summary, 5 exit. If you want a student-facing cue, add a one-line share prompt before `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:236`.
At `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:126`, replace the current heading with “Apply -- Make Sense and Persevere.”

Tighten Do Now C without giving away the answer. Keep the main prompt, but add a short hint after `tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:114`: “Name the excluded x-value and what in the expression would make that value impossible.”

Section D — VERDICT.verdict: Ship after fixing the exit, the Savvas-traceability drift in #35/#36, and the earlier ELL scaffolds.
Section D — VERDICT.justification: The packet already satisfies most of the visible OBS-template constraints: centered title and 3-row table (`tex/L43_P1_obs_student.tex:42-70`), one section per page (`:119`, `:182`, `:236`), Name-before-Exit (`:245-248`), and reflection prompts (`:266-277`). The remaining problems are real, but they are surgical, not structural.
